title: Firstmile founder brief and all-staff slate v0.1
content:
Purpose and intent:
This is a compact founder-facing brief plus the all-staff run-of-show seed for the "First Mile" company focus week (two-week orientation + one all-hands). Goal: land the narrative, lock company-level OKRs for Q2, and surface hard tradeoffs for resourcing prior to exec sign-off.

Top-line thesis for message to staff (for founders to validate):
- We are shifting from scale experiments to predictable, operationally-owned product outcomes: throughput, cost-per-token, and enterprise readiness.
- The next 90 days are about finishing instrumentation, stabilizing rollout paths, and creating visible win metrics for customers.

Who this doc is for: founders (Jeff/Maya), execs, and the all-staff program committee. Use as pre-read for Friday founders sync.

Anchor company OKR draft (proposal to discuss, one objective with three measurable results each):
1) Objective: Make inference predictable for production teams (reduce surprise, increase throughput predictability)
   KR1.1: Reduce 95th-percentile latency variance by 25% on hosted API (end-to-end wall clock)
   KR1.2: Ship prefix/KV caching defaults and enablement docs; 40% of production traffic using cache profiles
   KR1.3: Customer-facing SLOs (latency + availability) published and accepted by 3 pilot enterprise customers

2) Objective: Lower unit cost where it matters (practical wins for mid-market customers)
   KR2.1: Achieve 18% average token cost reduction across top-10 hosted models via batching + quantization recommendations
   KR2.2: Launch Redwood Optimize beta (cost/profile suggestions) with 5 paying beta customers
   KR2.3: Document and automate one repeatable autoscale pattern that reduces peak GPU idle time by 30%

3) Objective: Reduce risk and ramp for Private deployments
   KR3.1: Deliver VPC private-control plane alpha and one air-gapped test runbook
   KR3.2: Integrate with two KMS providers and pass internal compliance checklist
   KR3.3: Ship on-prem install blueprint and validated test (customer lab) for a 6-node minimum configuration

Notes on these OKRs (working):
- These are intentionally operational and productized. We need one additional 'moonshot' OKR if founders want aspirational signal.
- Metrics ownership: add primary owners after founder review. Right now engineering-sre and product-hosted-api are the obvious leads.

Founder-facing executive update (one-pager talk track):
- Quick wins (30s each): shipping default cache profiles, Optimize beta go/no-go, first private-control-plane alpha deploy
- Risks (30s): capacity tightness if QPS rises 50% during peak, customer SLA negotiation timeline, unknowns with quantized model quality regressions
- Ask (30s): decision on re-allocating one senior infra SWE from runtime to private-deployments (6-week redeploy) and commitment to $X reserved capacity buy for Dedicated pilots

All-hands run-of-show (90 minutes) — draft:
- 00:00–00:05 Intro (Founders — Jeff): narrative arc and why First Mile matters
- 00:05–00:15 State of the product (CTO — Maya): 3 slides: throughput, cost trends, reliability
- 00:15–00:30 Customer story (CS lead — Jonah): pilot customer wins + live quote clip (30s)
- 00:30–00:45 OKR reveal & context (Product — Priya): present proposed company OKRs, invite reactions
- 00:45–01:00 Breakouts (team micro-sessions): working promises and commitments (templates attached below)
- 01:00–01:15 Breakout reports (rep from each cluster): 3 key commitments + blockers
- 01:15–01:25 Founders close (Q&A live, moderated)

Facilitation notes and mechanics:
- Breakouts: 8 rooms, 12 people max, one notetaker (template: "Commitment / Owner / Riskiest Assumption / By-when"). Collect notes to Slack + confluence page.
- Pre-reads: founders want 2x page executive pre-read. Keep the pre-read under 800 words. Send 48h before event.
- Tech: stream to recording; ensure captions and remote Q&A (Slido).

Checklist (prep owners):
- Priya: finalize OKR numbers and owner suggestions (due: 2026-02-18)
- Jonah: customer story clip + legal approval (due: 2026-02-20)
- SRE lead (Diego): capacity slide and 95th-percentile baseline (due: 2026-02-17)
- Maya: CTO state deck (2 slides + script) (due: 2026-02-20)
- Ops: room assignments + breakout facilitators (due: 2026-02-22)

Open questions we need founders to decide this week (priority order):
1) Reallocate senior infra SWE to Private (risk: slows runtime feature progress) — founders YES/NO
2) Approve $Reserved pilot commitment for Dedicated (yes/no + budget cap)
3) Accept proposed KR thresholds or push for more ambitious cost targets?

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: OKRs too conservative -> morale signal low. Mitigation: add a visible moonshot OKR and pair with recognition program.
- Risk: Quantization regressions cause customer pushback. Mitigation: flag a rollback policy and include quality guardrails in Optimize beta.
- Risk: All-hands feels like "ask-heavy". Mitigation: dedicate 20% of time to celebration/customer stories and success signals.

Decision log (placeholder) — fill after founders sync:
- [ ] founder decision on infra reassign
- [ ] reserved capacity approval
- [ ] final OKR sign-off

Next steps (immediate):
- Share this doc as pre-read to founders and execs by EOD Tuesday (Priya)
- Ops to publish meeting invite and Slido link (Ops)
- Collect final owner nominations from leads (by 2026-02-16)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep language simple — "predictable inference" resonates more than "platform efficiency" in customer stories.
- We should bake an internal "war-room" page for the week with live SLO dashboards. Ask observability for a temporary 72h dashboard snapshot.
- If founders push for bolder cost savings, we will need a model-quality test harness included in Optimize beta scope.

Attachments referenced: commitment template (sheet), breakouts roster (sheet), pre-read one-pager (slides).

End of brief.

Revision history:
- v0.1 2026-02-10 Priya initial draft
- v0.2 2026-02-25 Priya + Jonah: added customer clip notes and breakout mechanics"
